tagline: Along a beach the glacial lake left high and dry.
intro: From Becks Road the parkway works east across the hills of Duluth for 28 miles to Seven Bridges Road, keeping to the old shoreline of Glacial Lake Duluth. The glacial lake drained away long ago. What the road looks down on now is the harbor, the St. Louis River bay and Lake Superior.

William K. Rogers, the city's first park board president, had it started on Tenth Street in April 1889, and by August it was in use. It went by Terrace Parkway, The Boulevard, Lake View Terrace and a few other names until a newspaper contest in 1929 settled on Skyline.

moments.title: Stewart Creek Bridge
moments.text: A single stone arch of dark green gabbro carries the road over a deep ravine on a secluded bend, its railings topped with a double sawtooth of rock.

moments.title: Enger Tower
moments.text: Crown Prince Olav of Norway dedicated this 80-foot stone tower on Enger Hill in 1939, and 72 years later his son, King Harald, came to dedicate it again.

moments.title: Hawk Ridge
moments.text: Birds of prey coming south from Canada would rather not cross Lake Superior, so they follow the shore and funnel over this ridge, where the Duluth Bird Club began counting them in 1951.

practical: Between Stewart Creek and Becks Road the parkway is unpaved, and from Magney-Snively Park to Becks Road it is closed to cars in winter, open then only to snowmobiles, bikes and foot traffic.
